actions.name: petrifying gaze
actions.desc: If a creature starts its turn within 30 feet of the [[lookup @name lowercase]]{monster} and the two of them can see each other, the [[lookup @name lowercase]]{monster} can force the creature to make a [[/save]] saving throw if the [[lookup @name lowercase]]{monster} isn't &reference[incapacitated apply=false]. On a failed save, the creature magically begins to turn to stone and is &reference[restrained]. It must repeat the saving throw at the end of its next turn. On a success, the effect ends. On a failure, the creature is &reference[petrified] until freed by the @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells.Item.WzvJ7G3cqvIubsLk]{greater restoration} spell or other magic. A creature that isn't &reference[surprise]{Surprised} can avert its eyes to avoid the saving throw at the start of its turn. If it does so, it can't see the [[lookup @name lowercase]]{monster} until the start of its next turn, when it can avert its eyes again. If it looks at the [[lookup @name lowercase]]{monster} in the meantime, it must immediately make the save. If the [[lookup @name lowercase]]{monster} sees its reflection within 30 feet of it in &reference[bright light], it mistakes itself for a rival and targets itself with its gaze.
